title: Service account usage metering and rotation flow (draft)
content:
Purpose:
This is an early draft exploring a combined UX for service account lifecycle: creation, scoped API key issuance, usage metering (per-key and per-service-account), and key rotation/expiry flows. We want a single console surface where admins can both understand how service accounts are being used in their org and take low-friction actions (rotate, revoke, limit scopes).

Context and problem statement:
- Customers have asked for clearer visibility into how service accounts are used across projects and pipelines. Current console pages scatter info across: service account creation, a separate API key listing, and the org audit log.
- Operators want the ability to rotate keys with minimal disruption and to see last-used timestamps so they can retire idle keys.
- Security/compliance teams want audit-ready timelines and an exportable report for rotations and revocations.

Primary goals for this design:
1) One-page view per service account summarizing keys, scopes, last-used, and telemetry links.
2) Make rotation a one-click operation with optional staged rollout (create new key -> swap -> revoke old key) and rollback path.
3) Show usage in a compact timeline and quick filters (today, 7d, 30d, by model/route).
4) Provide a lightweight metering table that maps tokens/requests to per-key usage for billing and anomaly detection.

Audience & personas:
- Platform engineer (admin): needs to rotate and revoke keys, set TTL policies, and export audit history.
- App developer (owner of a service account): needs to see which keys are used by which environments and request scoped keys.
- Security reviewer: wants to see rotation cadence, policy enforcement, and a tamper-evident timeline.

Wireframe notes (high level):
- Top bar: Service account name, description, owner(s), environment tag (prod/staging), linked repos/services.
- Action strip (right-aligned): Create scoped key, Rotate all keys, Set TTL/policy, Export audit CSV.
- Main pane split: Left 60% = Keys & actions; Right 40% = Usage timeline + quick audit.

Left pane: Keys & actions (components)
- Key list (table rows): Key name (human-friendly), key id (short), scope (routes/models), created at, last used (human relative), status (active/expired/revoked), usage bucket (small sparkbars inline).
- Per-row actions: Copy key (only once view for secret), Create rotated key, Revoke, Attach policy, Show requester list (which service or IP used it).
- Multi-select toolbar: Bulk revoke, Bulk rotate (creates new keys and maps to replacement operation), Download key manifest (audit).
- Create scoped key modal: Inputs: name, scopes (autocomplete by model/route), TTL (1h/24h/30d/custom), IP allowlist (optional), notify on first use (checkbox). UX note: scaffold suggested presets for "read-only embeddings" and "prod inference".

Right pane: Usage timeline + quick audit
- Metric bar (top): total requests, tokens used, error rate, tokens per request (7d). Clicking any metric filters both timeline and key table.
- Compact timeline: stacked area showing top 3 keys by requests; hover opens small tooltip with example request metadata (route, region). Timeline default = 30d.
- Quick audit list (reverse-chron): key creation, rotations, revocations, policy changes. Each item is tappable and links to full audit event in audit-log view (new window). Include a small badge for items with policy mismatches.
- Export & retention settings link: opens modal for CSV export filters and retention policies.

Rotation flow (sketch):
- Intent: Rotation should be safe and reversible. Admin chooses: "Create replacement and schedule revoke" or "Immediate rotate (swap)".
- Implementation stub UX: 1) Admin selects a key, clicks Rotate -> modal asks for scratch name for replacement; select whether to update linked secrets (automated via CI/CD integration) or leave manual. 2) Console creates new key and displays ephemeral secret with big copy button and admonition to store. 3) Option to auto-toggle traffic via Redwood routing: "Swap now" will gate new key as primary for routing decisions (only for keys used via SDK with key id metadata). 4) Schedule revoke: choose delay (e.g., 24h, 7d) or revoke after successful heartbeat seen.

Edge cases and unresolved decisions:
- How do we detect which deployments use a given key? We can surface top request origins by IP or by token-carrying client metadata but we do not have perfect mapping to repo/CI. Need infra input (Benji).
- Auto-swap capability requires an update to routing metadata and per-request key identifiers. Might be limited to Hosted API and Dedicated with Redwood routing enabled. Clarify with infra team.
- What is the retention policy for last-used timestamps? GDPR considerations: we may need to purge older detailed requester metadata. Add to security review.
- Export format: CSV vs. signed PDF for compliance. Security wants tamper evidence (hashes).

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- Per-service-account page shows all keys, last-used, and allows single-key rotation and revoke.
- Create scoped keys with TTL and IP allowlist in modal.
- Timeline shows requests by key for last 30 days and supports metric filters (tokens, requests).
- Audit export (CSV) available for selected date range.

Future / stretch ideas:
- Integrate with Secrets Manager: one-click push of new rotated key to supported providers (AWS Secrets Manager, GCP Secret Manager, HashiCorp Vault).
- Automated rotation policy: allow org-level policy to enforce rotation cadence and default TTLs; console surfaces offending keys.
- Anomaly detection: flag unusual spikes in key usage and surface remediation recipes (limit scope, rotate).

Links to related console surfaces and tickets:
- Existing service account creation flow: ticket PROJ-1110 (needs to hook into this page).
- Audit log v2 (work in progress): Confluence page linked above.
- Metric pipeline: engineering/observability task OBS-77 for per-key telemetry ingestion.

Open questions for next sync (owner: Asha):
- Product decision: Do we make auto-swap opt-in per-org or per-service-account? Recommendation: per-org boolean behind feature flag for now.
- Security: acceptable retention window for request-level metadata? (Marta to confirm).
- Engineering: feasibility of per-key routing swap; if not feasible, fall back to manual copy & replace path (Owen).

Notes from guerrilla testing (quick hallway feedback):
- "Show last-used in minutes" is helpful for SREs when rotating, but noise for long-lived infra keys. Suggest tooltip and a filter to hide keys not used in X days.
- Developers like the idea of presets in "Create scoped key" modal. Add a tiny library of common presets and ability to create org presets.

Immediate next steps (this week):
- Sync with Benji (infra) and Owen (SD) to validate swap capability and telemetry requirements.
- Create low-fidelity wireframes for the per-account page and rotation modal (Marta).
- Draft JIRA epic and split into stories: view page, create key modal, rotation flow, timeline visualization, export.

Appendix: low-fi wireframe notes (for designer)
- Canvas A (Service account page): header -- name | tags | owner; below left = vertical table of keys; right column = small stacked area chart over 30d; below = audit list; floating action = + Create scoped key.
- Canvas B (Rotate modal): big warning banner, input: replacement name, checkbox: attempt auto-swap, TTL, schedule revoke after X, confirm. After creation show ephemeral secret; CTA: Copy & Done; link to docs for programmatic rotation.

Document history:
- 2024-11-15 created by Asha Kapoor.
- 2024-11-22 internal review notes added from Benji and Marta.
- 2024-12-05 updated to include acceptance criteria and next steps.
